---
title: "Lab 00 — Setting Up"
subtitle: "R, Quarto and VS Code, and proving they actually work"
---

# Overview

Before any of the analysis labs will run, you need three things on your machine
and — the part that catches nearly everyone — your terminal needs to be able to
find them.

This lab is not analysis. It is plumbing. Work through it in order and do not skip
the checkpoints: each one tells you whether the previous step actually worked,
which is much cheaper than discovering it in the middle of Lab 01.

Budget about forty minutes, most of which is waiting for downloads.

| Tool | What it does | Do you need it? |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **R** | The language that does the analysis | Yes |
| **Quarto** | Turns a document containing R code into a web page | Yes |
| **VS Code** | The editor you write in | Yes |
| **RStudio** | An alternative editor, built specifically for R | Optional |

::: {.callout-note}
## If you would rather use RStudio

RStudio bundles Quarto and needs less setup than VS Code. If you already have it
and are happy in it, install R (Step 1), skip Steps 3 and 4, and go straight to
the checkpoints. Everything in the analysis labs works identically. This sheet
uses VS Code because that is what the module demonstrates.
:::

---

# Step 1 — Install R

**Windows.** Download from [cran.r-project.org](https://cran.r-project.org) →
*Download R for Windows* → *base* → *Download R x.x.x for Windows*. Run the
installer and accept the defaults.

**macOS.** Same site → *Download R for macOS* → the `.pkg` matching your chip
(Apple silicon or Intel).

::: {.callout-warning}
## The Windows R installer does not add R to your PATH

This is deliberate on their part and inconvenient for everyone. Step 4 fixes it.
Do not skip Step 4 just because the installer said it finished successfully.
:::

# Step 2 — Install Quarto

Download the installer for your platform from
[quarto.org/docs/get-started](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started) and run it.

On Windows you can also use:

```powershell
winget install --id Posit.Quarto
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Do not rely on the copy inside RStudio

RStudio ships its own private copy of Quarto at a path like
`C:\Program Files\RStudio\resources\app\bin\quarto\bin`. It works, but it is tied
to your RStudio version and moves when RStudio updates. Install Quarto properly.
:::

# Step 3 — Install VS Code and two extensions

Download VS Code from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com).

Then open the Extensions panel (`Ctrl+Shift+X`, or `Cmd+Shift+X` on macOS) and
install:

| Extension | Publisher | What it gives you |
| :- | :- | :- |
| **Quarto** | Posit | Syntax highlighting for `.qmd`, a Render button, live preview |
| **R** | REditorSupport | R syntax highlighting and a console inside the editor |

# Step 4 — Make your terminal find them

This is the step that causes almost every problem people report. Two separate
things go wrong.

## Your PATH may not include R

Open a terminal in VS Code with `` Ctrl+` `` and run:

```powershell
Rscript --version
```

If that reports a version, skip to the next heading. If it says *not recognized*,
find your R installation and add it:

```powershell
Get-ChildItem "C:\Program Files\R"
```

Take the folder name it reports — something like `R-4.4.1` — and substitute it
below:

```powershell
[Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("Path", $env:Path + ";C:\Program Files\R\R-4.4.1\bin", "User")
```

## Your terminal is holding a stale copy of PATH

A terminal keeps the environment it started with, and **VS Code hands every new
terminal a cached copy**. So after installing anything, a brand new terminal panel
will still not see it.

To refresh the terminal you are in right now:

```powershell
$env:Path = [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","Machine") + ";" + [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable("Path","User")
```

To fix it permanently, **close VS Code completely** — every window, not *Reload
Window* — and reopen it.

::: {.callout-note}
## macOS and Linux

Both installers put R and Quarto on your PATH without help. If a command is not
found, close the terminal and open a new one, and if that fails, restart VS Code.
:::

---

# Checkpoint 1 — Are the tools visible?

Run all three in a VS Code terminal:

```powershell
quarto --version
Rscript --version
code --version
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="What you should see"}
Three version numbers. Quarto should be **1.4 or later** and R **4.3 or later**.

If any command is *not recognized*, go back to Step 4. Do not continue — nothing
below will work.
:::

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="PowerShell: why `R --version` fails even when R works"}
`R` is a built-in PowerShell alias for `Invoke-History`, so `R --version` never
reaches your R installation. You will see a confusing error mentioning
*"Cannot locate the history for command line"*.

Use `Rscript --version` instead, or `R.exe --version` to bypass the alias.
`Rscript` is the one that matters anyway — it is what Quarto calls.
:::

# Step 5 — Install the R packages

```powershell
Rscript -e "install.packages(c('readr','knitr'), repos='https://cloud.r-project.org')"
```

Those two are all the labs need. Accept any prompt about a personal library.

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true" title="PowerShell mangles quotes — use the right ones"}
Note the quoting above: **double quotes outside, single quotes inside**. PowerShell
strips double quotes when passing arguments to a program, so the reverse
arrangement arrives at R as `install.packages(c(readr,knitr), repos=https:/)` and
fails with `unexpected '/'`.
:::

# Step 6 — Get the project and the data

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/nmcguinness/L8-3DGD-Playtest-Analytics.git
cd L8-3DGD-Playtest-Analytics
code .
```

No Git? Use the green **Code** button on the repository page →
*Download ZIP*, then unzip it and open the folder in VS Code with *File → Open
Folder*.

The `data/` folder contains the five CSVs every lab uses.

---

# Checkpoint 2 — Render something

Create a new file called `test.qmd` in the project folder with exactly this
content:

```` markdown
---
title: "Setup test"
---

## Does R work?

```{{r}}
library(readr)
sessions <- read_csv("data/tidebreak_sessions.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
nrow(sessions)
```

## Does plotting work?

```{{r}}
hist(sessions$score, breaks = 20, main = "Score", xlab = "Score")
```
````

Then render it:

```powershell
quarto render test.qmd
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="What success looks like"}
The terminal reports `Output created: test.html`. Open that file in a browser and
you should see the number **120** and a histogram.

If you see both, everything works and you are ready for Lab 01. Delete `test.qmd`
and `test.html`.
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true" title="If the render fails"}
Work through these in order.

**`could not find function "read_csv"`** — Step 5 did not complete. Re-run it and
watch for errors.

**`cannot open file 'data/tidebreak_sessions.csv'`** — you are not in the project
folder, or `test.qmd` is not beside the `data/` folder. Run `Get-Location` to see
where you are and `Get-ChildItem data` to confirm the CSVs are there.

**`Unable to locate an installed version of R`** — Quarto cannot find R. This is
Step 4. Confirm `Rscript --version` works *in the same terminal* you are rendering
from.

**No error, but nothing happens** — you are probably in a terminal that Claude or
another process is using. Open a second terminal with the `+` button in the
terminal panel.
:::

---

# Troubleshooting reference

Keep this. Every one of these has bitten someone on this module.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
| :- | :- | :- |
| `'quarto' is not recognized` | PATH not refreshed since install | Refresh line in Step 4, then restart VS Code fully |
| `'Rscript' is not recognized` | Windows R installer does not set PATH | Step 4, first half |
| `R : Cannot locate the history for command line` | `R` is a PowerShell alias for `Invoke-History` | Use `Rscript` or `R.exe` |
| `unexpected '/' in "install.packages..."` | PowerShell stripped your double quotes | Double outside, single inside |
| Command works in one terminal, not a new one | VS Code caches the environment per terminal | Close VS Code entirely and reopen |
| `Unable to locate an installed version of R` | Quarto cannot see R on PATH | Step 4, then check in the *same* terminal |
| Render works, but a plot is missing | The chunk is `{r}` with a typo, or the code errored above it | Read the terminal output from the top; the first error is the real one |
| `Error in library(x) : there is no package called 'x'` | Package not installed for *this* R version | Re-run Step 5; check `Rscript --version` matches the R you installed |

---

# What to do if you are still stuck

Post in the module forum with **all three** of the following, or nobody can help
you:

1. The exact command you ran
2. The complete error message, copied as text rather than a screenshot
3. The output of `quarto --version` and `Rscript --version`

The third one resolves about half of these on its own.
